issues.reason: The exact InitialState alternatives are distinct by trigger, but the closed representation exposes the conditions as triggers rather than guard expressions. The contrastive guard-disjointness property is therefore not expressible by the frozen finite-domain predicate without a supplied domain.
issues.requirement_quote: based on conditions: `high_way=true` for HighwayMode or `urban_way=true` for UrbanMode
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Distinct exact triggers may provide operational distinction even though the frozen V1 predicate cannot evaluate the source-side guard formulation.
issues.title: Highway alternatives share one condition

issues.basis: NL3 transition group and closed transitions lines 24 and 25, each triggered by dist_to_front_25_extra_lane_true.
issues.expected: The cruise and lane_change alternatives from enter_hwy are distinguishable by their stated conditions.
issues.observed: Both closed alternatives use the same trigger and have no parsed guard.
issues.reason: Both exact enter_hwy alternatives target different states but carry the same effective closed trigger, so the alternatives are operationally indistinguishable under the supplied condition relation.
issues.requirement_quote: based on the distance to the front vehicle (`dist_to_front<25`) and the availability of an extra lane (`extra_lane=true`)
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source itself states the same conjunction for both targets, so the supplied author condition may intentionally permit nondeterministic alternatives rather than require exclusive guards.
issues.title: Highway entry alternatives collide

issues.basis: NL7, source transition tr_0013, and closed transition line 42.
issues.observed: UrbanMode initial transition line 42 reaches enter_urban with no trigger.
issues.reason: The exact UrbanMode-owned initial edge reaches enter_urban and is untriggered, so this contract is satisfied. However, the closed model also has a separate conditional root entry defect, which does not alter this owner-local fact.
issues.requirement_quote: the system begins in the enter_urban substate
issues.strongest_rebuttal: No supplied fact rebuts the exact owner-local edge.
issues.title: Urban mode initial entry is unguarded

issues.basis: NL6 termination contract; transition:line:59; state:FinishState:line:58; LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING and reachable termination-target facts.
issues.expected: HighwayMode should terminate at FinishState as a stable completion state.
issues.observed: HighwayMode reaches FinishState, and FinishState is reachable but has no outgoing FCSTM transition.
issues.reason: The required HighwayMode-to-FinishState endpoint exists, but the exact target is a reachable leaf with no outgoing FCSTM transition. The finite frontier therefore shows that entry to FinishState does not establish stable termination of the enclosing HighwayMode.
issues.requirement_quote: The HighwayMode ends when the system transitions to FinishState
issues.strongest_rebuttal: FinishState may intentionally be the final global state; however, the supplied termination contract specifically identifies HighwayMode ending at FinishState, while the deterministic fact only establishes a leaf with no outgoing transition and does not prove enclosing composite completion semantics.
issues.title: HighwayMode does not stably terminate

issues.basis: NL10 termination contract; transition:line:60; state:FinishState:line:58; reachable leaf frontier fact.
issues.expected: UrbanMode should terminate at FinishState as a stable completion state.
issues.observed: UrbanMode reaches FinishState, and FinishState is reachable but has no outgoing FCSTM transition.
issues.reason: The required UrbanMode-to-FinishState endpoint exists, but the shared reachable FinishState target has no outgoing FCSTM transition. Endpoint existence therefore does not close the stronger stable-termination obligation.
issues.requirement_quote: The system exits the UrbanMode state by transitioning to FinishState
issues.strongest_rebuttal: A leaf FinishState could be an intended terminal state, but the supplied obligation is about UrbanMode terminating, not merely having an edge to a leaf, and no deterministic closure fact proves that the enclosing mode is completed.
issues.title: UrbanMode does not stably terminate

issues.basis: NL3 group contract and transition group; source transitions tr_0006/tr_0007; closed transitions transition:line:24 and transition:line:25 both triggered by dist_to_front_25_extra_lane_true with empty guards.
issues.expected: The cruise and lane_change alternatives from enter_hwy should retain distinct stated condition roles.
issues.observed: Both alternatives use the same closed-model trigger and have no parsed guards, while the source group describes condition roles involving front distance and extra-lane availability.
issues.reason: Both exact enter_hwy alternatives are present, but both carry the same effective trigger and neither has a distinct guard. The model therefore cannot preserve the source distinction between cruise and lane_change conditions; the precise group property is not represented by a frozen predicate.
issues.requirement_quote: The enter_hwy transition alternatives must retain their stated condition roles.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source may intentionally express the conjunction as one opaque event; even under that reading, the two alternatives remain operationally indistinguishable, and the closed model supplies no separate condition relation.
issues.title: Highway entry alternatives are indistinguishable

issues.basis: NL12 group contract; source transition tr_0024; closed carrier transition:line:72 and its single combined trigger; working-contract compiler boundary.
issues.expected: The activation transition should retain the stated pedestrian, rear-risk, and mode-specific front-risk condition alternatives.
issues.observed: The closed model has one combined trigger on transition:line:72, with no parsed guard or separate alternative consumers.
issues.reason: The exact deactive-to-active transition exists and carries one opaque trigger whose source text combines the alternatives. The closed model does not expose independent event/guard projections for the pedestrian, rear-risk, and mode-specific front-risk alternatives, so the precise condition-role obligation remains a semantic gap.
issues.requirement_quote: The deactive-to-active transition must retain the stated activation condition alternatives.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The combined trigger text could be treated as an equivalent opaque event, but the supplied obligation explicitly preserves separate activation alternatives and the closed typed inventory does not expose those distinctions for behavioral comparison.
